system.boundary: Build a full passenger-vehicle braking model in Simulink or Simscape.
engineering_objects: The physical plant must include a finite-mass vehicle body with coupled longitudinal, lateral, yaw, roll, pitch and heave motion, four suspension and wheel paths, four distinct tire-road contacts, a powertrain capable of accelerating the vehicle, and four independently actuated wheel brakes.
The vehicle trajectory must result from the connected body, suspension, wheel, tire, driveline and brake dynamics;
When UseLowFrictionPatch is true, apply RoadFrictionScaleLow inside the supplied rectangular spatial region and RoadFrictionScaleHigh outside it, according to each wheel's physical contact location.
physical_paths: The vehicle trajectory must result from the connected body, suspension, wheel, tire, driveline and brake dynamics; prescribed chassis motion, replayed outputs, duplicated wheel channels and open-loop braking are not valid solutions.
Measurements must come from the connected physical and control paths that determine vehicle motion.

interfaces.name: TargetSpeed_mps
interfaces.description: MATLAB base-workspace input declared by the current public task contract.
interfaces.range_or_shape: Accelerate in a straight line toward TargetSpeed_mps and begin the commanded braking maneuver after the vehicle reaches BrakeStartDistance_m. Read TargetSpeed_mps, BrakeStartDistance_m, RequestedDeceleration_g, RoadFrictionScaleHigh, RoadFrictionScaleLow, UseLowFrictionPatch and LowFrictionPatch_m from the MATLAB base workspace. TargetSpeed_mps is a real scalar in [16, 22] m/s; BrakeStartDistance_m is a real scalar in [160, 220] m; RequestedDeceleration_g is a positive real scalar in [0.2, 0.5] g; RoadFrictionScaleHigh and RoadFrictionScaleLow are real scalars in [0.5, 0.8] and [0.2, 0.5], respectively, as dimensionless tire-friction scaling factors; UseLowFrictionPatch is a scalar logical; and LowFrictionPatch_m is a 1-by-4 real vector in m ordered [region start X, region start Y, region length in X, region width in Y].

interfaces.name: VehicleState
interfaces.description: Output container declared by the current public task contract.
interfaces.range_or_shape: Log complete-run MATLAB Timeseries named VehicleState, WheelState, BrakeState, and TireForceState. VehicleState has 8 channels in this order: longitudinal position X (m), lateral position Y (m), longitudinal and lateral body speed (m/s), longitudinal and lateral body acceleration (m/s^2), yaw angle (rad), and yaw rate (rad/s).

interfaces.name: WheelState
interfaces.description: Output container declared by the current public task contract.
interfaces.range_or_shape: Log complete-run MATLAB Timeseries named VehicleState, WheelState, BrakeState, and TireForceState. WheelState has 12 channels in FL, FR, RL, RR order within each group: four wheel angular speeds (rad/s), four effective rolling radii (m), and four longitudinal slip ratios (1).

interfaces.name: BrakeState
interfaces.description: Output container declared by the current public task contract.
interfaces.range_or_shape: Log complete-run MATLAB Timeseries named VehicleState, WheelState, BrakeState, and TireForceState. BrakeState has 12 channels in FL, FR, RL, RR order within each group: four commanded brake pressures, four measured brake pressures, and four ABS-active flags.

interfaces.name: TireForceState
interfaces.description: Output container declared by the current public task contract.
interfaces.range_or_shape: Log complete-run MATLAB Timeseries named VehicleState, WheelState, BrakeState, and TireForceState. TireForceState has 8 channels in FL, FR, RL, RR order within each group: four longitudinal and four lateral tire forces (N).
